title: Regular finite stages and parameter quotients in an ind-etale henselian lift
statement: Let $B$ be a regular Noetherian ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, $r\geq0$, and set $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Assume that for every prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq J$ the tuple $(t_i)$ in $B_{\mathfrak p}$ extends to a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $B\to C$ be an ind-etale map [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] with $C$ Noetherian and $\operatorname{Spec}C$ nonempty connected, and suppose $JC$ is contained in every maximal ideal of $C$. Then $C$ is a regular domain. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C$, the tuple $(t_i)$ is a regular sequence in $C_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and $C_{\mathfrak m}/(t_i)$ is a nonzero regular local ring. More precisely, for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $B$ the fibre $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_B C$ is reduced and every localization at a prime of that fibre is a field; in particular all the fibres are regular. The same conclusions hold when $r=0$.

proof.text: Transport IndEtaleAcrossUniverses to weak etaleness via RingHom.IndEtale.weaklyEtale on the canonical ULift map and Mathlib Algebra.WeaklyEtale.ulift_iff. This gives flatness. For each prime p, the residue-field base-change instance gives a weakly etale algebra F = kappa(p) tensor_B C. The proved source theorem Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul' applied to Algebra.WeaklyEtale.flat_lmul' makes F absolutely flat. This uses only flatness of tensor multiplication, exactly the first paragraph of the proof of Stacks 092Q.

Apply the proved source absolutely-flat API in WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.WeakDimension: its IsReduced instance gives reducedness of F, and Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.isField_of_isLocalization_prime gives IsField for each F_Q. These declarations are universe-polymorphic, include the zero fibre vacuously, and implement Stacks 092F and 092I, used in the first paragraph of Tag 092Q. No finite-etale-subalgebra or finite-product classification is needed.

proof.text: The fibre $F$ is Noetherian: the fibre-ring presentation identifies it with a quotient of the localization of $C$ at the image of $B\setminus\mathfrak p$, and Noetherianity passes to both that localization and its quotient. Each $F_Q$ is a field by step 2, hence is regular local: its maximal ideal is zero, its dimension is zero, and the empty family generates its maximal ideal. Thus $F$ is a regular Noetherian ring. This also includes $F=0$, whose regularity condition has no primes to check.

Apply regular-map ascent to $B\to C$: the source is regular by hypothesis, the target is Noetherian by hypothesis, the map is flat by step 1, and every fibre is regular by step 3. It follows that $C$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre), applied at each target prime

proof.text: The affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is regular by the definition of regularity and step 4. It is nonempty and connected by hypothesis. The regular-connected-integral theorem makes $X$ integral. Taking its nonempty affine open $X$ itself in the definition of an integral scheme shows that $C$ is an integral domain. Together with step 4 this proves that $C$ is a regular domain.

Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset C$, and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m\cap B$, $R=B_{\mathfrak p}$, $S=C_{\mathfrak m}$. The flat-local-ring-map theorem gives a flat local map $R\to S$ of Noetherian local rings. The fibre prime correspondence supplies a prime $Q$ of $F=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_B C$ lying over $\mathfrak m$; the fibre-local-ring isomorphism identifies $S/\mathfrak pS$ with $F_Q$. By step 2 this quotient is a field. Since $\mathfrak pS\subseteq\mathfrak mS$ and $S$ is local, its being a field forces $\mathfrak pS=\mathfrak mS$. The local dimension equality in the flat height formula now gives $\dim S=\dim R+\dim(S/\mathfrak pS)=\dim R$. Moreover $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$: every $t_i$ maps into $JC\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Hence the assumed parameter condition applies at this precise prime $\mathfrak p$.

Extend $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ in $R$ to a full ordered regular system of parameters $(t_1,\ldots,t_r,x_{r+1},\ldots,x_d)$, where $d=\dim R$. Its images generate $\mathfrak pS=\mathfrak mS$, and their length is $d=\dim S$ by step 6. They therefore constitute a regular system of parameters in the regular local ring $S$. Apply the regular-local-generators theorem to this full list in $S$: it is a regular sequence and its initial quotient $S/(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ is regular local of dimension $d-r$. This quotient is nonzero because its defining ideal is contained in the proper maximal ideal $\mathfrak mS$. The multiplication-injectivity clauses for the first $r$ entries are among those for the full list; together with this nonzero quotient, the definition of regular sequence gives exactly that $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ is $S$-regular. For $r=0$ the same argument uses the empty initial list, whose quotient is $S$ itself and whose injectivity conditions are empty. No positive-length assumption has entered any earlier step.
